Possible sources for these deviations include: • Heat losses around the compressor and other HXs from the refrigerant to the surrounding ambient air, which may primarily relate to the thermal mass of the refrigerant. • Furthermore, sudden, noisy changes in the compressor suction and discharge conditions could be attributed to the slower experimental controls and slight leaks in the reversing valves within the experimental setup, which were not accounted for in these models. These reversing valves could also have slowed the migration of the refrigerant charge to the indoor components, thereby slowing the increase in indoor cooling capacity. • Some deviations were reported in the experimental TES inlet and outlet water temperatures, which could be due to more pronounced heat losses from PCM to surroundings when the compressor is off, or internal PCM heat conduction. Nonetheless, the overall system-level predictions were acceptable, with the maximum cooling capacity error less than 3%. The possible causes for these deviations include: • Slower experimental controls and slight leaks in the reversing valves within the experimental setup, which were not accounted for in these models. These reversing valves could also have caused the migration of refrigerant o charge from the indoor unit to the outdoor unit toward the end of the discharge process. This resulted in experimentally observed increases in discharge compressor pressure, leading to such differences. • Additionally, some deviations were reported in the experimental TES inlet and outlet water temperatures. These deviations could be due to more pronounced heat losses from the PCM to the surroundings when the compressor is off, internal PCM heat conduction, or heat transfer from the pumped water to the PCM.
